summary: Nine comment-endorsed finds spanning agent tools, media, motor control, games, robotics, and history.
telegram_footer: 9 items surfaced | 30/30 past-front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: GoModel
items.source_story_title: If you don't run your own LLM proxy, how do you know whats going on?
items.summary: Self-hosted LLM gateway with request labels, dashboards, and detailed agent-interaction history.
items.why_included: Strong first-hand home use plus a workplace rollout justify resurfacing beyond the 90-day cooldown.
items.evidence: A home user praises virtual models, arbitrary request labels, and dashboards, and says their workplace is rolling out the free version.

evidence_sources.author: verdverm
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use GoModel and its amazing. My favorite features are virtual model, the support for arbitrary request labels, and the nice dashboads / ui.

items.name: TermRover
items.source_story_title: Tmux and Claude Code: Sessions, Send-Keys, and the Ceiling
items.summary: Mobile SSH and Mosh terminal built around comfortable tmux session control.
items.why_included: A direct recommendation from a commenter describing their remote agent setup.
items.evidence: A commenter calls TermRover a pretty good SSH client for tmux.

evidence_sources.author: petesergeant
evidence_sources.excerpt: TermRover[1] is a pretty good SSH client for tmux.

items.name: Happier
items.source_story_title: Tmux and Claude Code: Sessions, Send-Keys, and the Ceiling
items.summary: Web and mobile front end for coding-agent sessions, praised for seamless Claude Code handover.
items.why_included: Positive first-hand use identifies a concrete way to move between terminal and mobile sessions.
items.evidence: A user describes Happier's web and iOS access and says handover with real Claude Code is seamless.

evidence_sources.author: petesergeant
evidence_sources.excerpt: For a more native integration I have started using Happier[2] which provides a web front-end and iOS app for my sessions too (unified with real Claude Code, so handover is seamless)

items.name: onion2k/guardrails
items.source_story_title: Ask HN: How to deal with shipping AI-written code you don't understand?
items.summary: Reusable testing skills for AI-generated code; its creator reports success across game projects.
items.why_included: A concrete repository with positive reported use, explicitly identified as creator evidence rather than independent validation.
items.evidence: The creator says the reusable guardrail skills have worked well across several game projects; they distinguish regression confidence from code quality or choosing the right change.

evidence_sources.author: onion2k
evidence_sources.excerpt: It might be the wrong change, and it might be crap code, but I can ship it without anything blowing up. I've been using it for a while across a few game projects and so far it's worked quite well.

items.name: Plezy
items.source_story_title: Plex vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild to drop a cryptominer
items.summary: Open-source Plex client praised as a UI replacement; one user reports a wake-navigation bug.
items.why_included: First-hand approval and a useful concrete caveat, with the product spelling resolved from a reply.
items.evidence: A user likes Plezy as an open-source Plex UI alternative but must press back after wake; a reply corrects the spelling to Plezy. It is a client replacement, not a server-security fix.

evidence_sources.author: HaloZero
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Pleezy which has been a nice open source alternative to the Plex UI. The only issue we've had is that on wake, you have to press back once to do anything else.

items.name: moteus
items.source_story_title: I built a drone with only one motor [video]
items.summary: Brushless motor controllers praised for build quality and helpful developer support.
items.why_included: Specific first-hand hardware praise from a satellite-tracking gimbal project, not just enthusiasm for the submitted drone.
items.evidence: A commenter used moteus controllers in a two-axis RF satellite-tracking gimbal and praises their quality and the lead developer's help.

evidence_sources.author: jcims
evidence_sources.excerpt: Side note, I used those same moteus controllers for a decidedly less energetic use case (two axis gimbal for RF satellite tracking) and found them to be super high quality and the lead developer always super helpful.

items.name: Human Resource Machine
items.source_story_title: It's still ok to enjoy programming
items.summary: Programming puzzle game about directing office workers; a recreational programmer says they loved it.
items.why_included: An explicit personal endorsement offers a playful detour from the thread's AI-and-work debate.
items.evidence: A commenter says they loved Human Resource Machine while finding 7 Billion Humans repetitive.

evidence_sources.author: xiaodai
evidence_sources.excerpt: I mean, I loved Human Resource Machine but not so much 7 billion humans (as the programming got repetitive).

items.name: Sebastian Thrun's DARPA Grand Challenge talk
items.summary: Google talk on autonomous driving, recommended for practical robot-training lessons and humor.
items.why_included: An explicit viewing recommendation highlights a concrete robotics talk rather than a generic topic.
items.evidence: A commenter praises the talk's discussion of robot training and highly recommends it as a funny time capsule of early self-driving research.

evidence_sources.author: alexpotato
evidence_sources.excerpt: Sebastian Thrun's talk at Google about winning the DARPA Grand Challenge [0] has a great discussion of training "robots".

items.name: Child Sacrifice in Ancient Israel
items.source_story_title: Ousted Savannah police officer gave ICE agent husband access to Flock system
items.summary: Historical study of ancient Israelite ritual, called a commenter's best book of the year.
items.why_included: A strong book endorsement hidden in an unrelated thread, with the linked DOI resolved to the publisher's title.
items.evidence: A commenter links this book and calls it the best book they read that year.

evidence_sources.author: everdrive
evidence_sources.excerpt: The best book I read this year was actually this (https://www.jstor.org/stable/10.5325/j.ctv2321hnd), so I'm aware (and was aware before) of human sacrifice.
